findings.title: Cache and health recommendations omit required structured provenance
findings.what: Both detectors return artifact-derived recommendation claims without a provenance object. Low-cache-hit states the affected-session count, threshold, overall average, and a token-touching reclaim fraction; low-health states the affected count and threshold-derived scores. Free-form detail/evidence does not provide the required structured source and field citations or reproducible inference trail.
findings.fix: Add provenance observations citing the relevant tokenData session totals/entries and computed values, plus an inference that states the threshold and derivation. Include an as-of/stale treatment if timestamps are available and the claims can become historical.
findings.acceptance: Construct firing recommendations for both detectors and assert validateRecommendationProvenance(rec) returns []; additionally assert observations identify the source artifact, exact tokenData fields, measured values, and threshold inference.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed both returned objects end without any provenance property; the cited claims are produced directly at low-cache-hit.ts:85-96 and low-health.ts:26-39.

findings.title: MCP schema savings can overcount heterogeneous per-session tool inventories
findings.what: The detector obtains each server's toolCount from aggregate cross-session statistics, then charges that full union count to every session merely containing the server (lines 111-127). If a server exposes different tool subsets across sessions, each session is billed for schemas observed only in other sessions, inflating estSavingsUsd. The user-facing claim at line 152 also says the schemas are cache-read every turn, while lines 124-127 explicitly model one cache-write followed by reads on only turns 2..N.
findings.fix: Retain per-session server tool counts from toolInventories and use those counts in sessionRedundantTokens. Change the detail to say the schemas are written once and cache-read on later turns.
findings.acceptance: Add a fixture where the same redundant server exposes different tool counts in two sessions and assert estSavingsUsd equals the sum of each session's own schema count times its write/read-turn pricing; assert the detail does not claim a cache read on the first turn.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read lines 99-127 and 145-152. The related baseline parser defines McpServerToolStats.toolCount as a distinct cross-session server footprint, confirming that line 117 reuses a union count per session; the existing tests use identical 30-tool inventories in both sessions and therefore do not expose the overcount.
